questions.question: How would you describe your physical stamina in everyday activities?

effects.safety: Non-diagnostic. Do not infer a cardiopulmonary diagnosis from low stamina alone.
effects.report: Higher limitation contributes to Energy & Vitality and can be interpreted with activity and respiratory answers.

questions.question: Which best describes your usual eating pattern?
options: Mostly whole and minimally processed foods
A mixture of whole and processed foods
Highly irregular or difficult to describe

effects.safety: Non-diagnostic. This is a broad dietary-pattern question and should not duplicate specific intake questions in scoring.
effects.report: Provides overall dietary context and may help explain more specific food-intake responses.

questions.question: When you do become unwell, how quickly do you usually recover?

effects.safety: Non-diagnostic. Slower recovery can have many causes.
effects.report: Higher values strengthen the Immune Resilience signal, particularly alongside Q02 and Q13.

questions.question: How often do you experience constipation, diarrhoea or other noticeable changes in bowel regularity?

effects.safety: Persistent, severe or concerning bowel changes should not be interpreted diagnostically by the quiz.
effects.report: Higher frequency contributes to Digestive & Gut Health.

questions.question: How often do you find it difficult to switch off or relax, even when you have the opportunity to do so?

effects.report: Higher frequency contributes to Mood, Stress & Emotional Balance and can support interpretation of sleep difficulty.

design_note: Q26 is now stamina only; respiratory symptoms are handled separately by Q45. Q27 is broad dietary context and should have limited weight because N03/N04/Q31 capture more specific intake. Q28 is the recovery-speed dimension of Immune Resilience. Q29 is a direct digestive signal. Q30 separates difficulty switching off from the broader stress question Q15.
